issues.description: HAS_TIME regex is an undocumented heuristic pre-filter that duplicates the parser's notion of "contains a time token".
issues.detail: The new /\dm?s/i guard short-circuits the valueParser walk, acting as a second implementation of the has-time predicate. Add a one-line comment naming it a cheap pre-filter and stating the invariant that it must stay in lockstep with the parser's unit list, so future time-unit additions update both sites.

issues.description: No regression test pins the early-return behavior against false negatives.
issues.detail: The patch is a behavior-preserving optimization, but nothing guards against the regex accidentally rejecting a real violation (odd whitespace, casing, vendor prefixes on the value side). A single test exercising an edge-case value that must still be flagged would lock in the fast-path contract. Not blocking.

synthesis.summary: The panel accepts this as a narrow, well-scoped performance fix: a cheap regex pre-filter short-circuits the valueParser walk in the time-min-milliseconds rule without weakening any contracts. Both reviewers converge on the same concern — the fast-path regex is an unstated second specification of "contains a time token" that must stay in sync with the authoritative parser. A one-line comment documenting the invariant (and ideally a regression test) is the only fixup requested. Verdict: land it with the trivial doc nit.
